AssemblerState.description: An assembler's retained state. Buffers are item-id → count maps.

craft_left.description: Ticks remaining in the current craft (`0` when not crafting).

inputs.description: The input buffer: item id → count (empty map when nothing buffered).

output.description: The output buffer: item id → count.

BeltItem.description: One item on a belt lane, as the JSON output spells it.

pos.description: Position in units from the lane's output end (`0..TILE`).

BeltState.description:
One belt's two lanes, each listing its items from the output end backward
(ascending `pos`).

left.description: The left lane (relative to the belt's direction of travel).

EntityState.description:
One entity's state, externally tagged so the array stays parallel to the
scenario's `entities` (`{ "belt": {...} }`, `{ "sink": {...} }`, …).

oneOf.description:
A source holds no item state at rest; `emit_phase` is `tick % period`, so
a mid-period snapshot is self-describing.
Empty-handed and back at the pickup, ready to grab.
Holding an item, counting the forward swing down.

Empty-handed, swinging back to the pickup after a drop (counting the return
down). The arm cannot grab again until the return completes, so the empty
return takes the same time as the loaded swing rather than being instant.

held.description: The held item, present only while swinging out.

swing_left.description:
Ticks remaining in the current motion — the forward swing while `swing`, the
empty return while `return`, and `0` while `idle`.

SinkState.description: A sink's retained state: per-item running consumed counts.

Snapshot.description: The complete canonical state at one snapshot tick.

checksum.description:
The FNV-1a checksum over the [canonical bytes](canonical_bytes) of this
snapshot, formatted `fnv1a64:%016x`. This is the validator's comparison
key.

entities.description: The per-entity state, in scenario placement order.

tick.description: The tick this snapshot was taken at.

SplitterState.description:
A splitter's retained state. A base splitter holds **no items between ticks**
(it transfers within the tick it pulls), so only its two cursors are retained:
the per-(item-type, lane) output-preference bitfield ([`SplitterState::out_pref`])
and the input-order cursor ([`SplitterState::in_first`]).

in_first.description:
Which input belt (`0`/`1`) the splitter tries first this tick (flips each tick
for input fairness).

out_pref.description:
The per-(item-type, lane) output alternation cursor: bit `t*2 + L` is the
output belt (`0`/`1`) the next item of item type `t` on lane `L` (`0` = left,
`1` = right) will be sent to (it flips after each such item). Keeping it per
lane balances each lane across both outputs; the input lane itself is preserved.
